verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpointing starts by default when the WAL reaches 1000 pages (about 4 MB). PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint ... zero or a negative value turns it off
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off ... enabled by default with an interval of 1000'; wal.html: 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE works like RESTART. On success it truncates the WAL file to zero bytes just before it returns.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'

verdicts.claim: Concurrent checkpoints on one file are mutually exclusive. A checkpoint that cannot get the checkpoint lock returns SQLITE_BUSY, and the busy handler is not called
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.'

verdicts.claim: A normal checkpoint does not truncate the WAL file ... journal_size_limit caps the file when it is set; its default is -1, which means no limit
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'in WAL mode, the write-ahead log file is not truncated following a checkpoint' and 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'

verdicts.claim: Litestream ... min-checkpoint-page-count defaults to 1000 pages and checkpoint-interval to 1 minute ... truncate-page-n, which defaults to 121359 pages (about 500 MB)
verdicts.evidence: guide: 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default', 'checkpoint-interval: 1m # Default: 1 minute', 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB'; passive-first fallback described

verdicts.claim: Litestream removed max-checkpoint-page-count in v0.5.0 because of safety concerns with RESTART checkpoints. truncate-page-n replaces it.
verdicts.evidence: config: 'The max-checkpoint-page-count field has been removed in v0.5.0 due to safety concerns with RESTART checkpoints. Use truncate-page-n instead.'

verdicts.claim: Tailscale recorded 19 corruption incidents over six months, starting in August 2025, before it found the cause.
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: '19 separate instances of database corruption over six months'; Register: 'in August 2025 those backups began detecting database corruption'

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug needs WAL mode, two or more connections ... SQLite says it likely affects releases 3.7.0 through 3.51.2.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09)'; 'two or more database connections open on the same file, in separate threads or processes'

verdicts.claim: SQLite identified and patched the WAL-reset bug on 2026-03-03. The fix ships in SQLite 3.51.3 (2026-03-13), with backports to 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed ... fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'
